sources.title: The King's Letter (manuscript plate)
sources.hand: J.R.R. Tolkien

text_held.why: Christopher Tolkien printed the text of this very manuscript, with a transliteration of both its English and its Sindarin, in HoME IX -- and said in the same breath exactly where the tengwar and the transliteration DISAGREE: the English transliteration omits Arathornsson and adds `day` where the tengwar read `the thirty-first of the Stirring`, and `and Arnor, ar Arnor` was added to both tengwar texts and is absent from both transliterations. All three copies are given, at t1_9_sauron_defeated.txt:4573-4630. So the archive is not owed a machine reading of the plate: it holds the Estate's own reading of it, including the variants an OCR pass could not have known were there. The .png remains what it always was -- a picture with no text layer, correctly extracting to nothing.

sources.attribution: J.R.R. Tolkien (manuscript; printed in Sauron Defeated)
